description.narrative: Mashambanzou Care Trust programme seeks to reduce the vulnerability of children in adversities as a result of poverty, HIV, TB and disability by providing socioeconomic and psychological support to families, the community. The programme specifically targets highly vulnerable and poor members of the community that include granny headed, child headed, orphans and other vulnerable children, female headed and other highly impoverished households. It raises awareness and promote children's rights as well as prioritizing children's need within health care. The programme also targets the poor communities especially those infected teenagers who have poor access to comprehensive sexual reproductive health and HIV services, partly due to stigma, insufficient support by health care workers, low-risk perception and economic disempowerment or poverty. This programme will seek to ensure reasonable sexual reproductive health by strengthening the institution’s provision of SRHR for both infected young men and young women to increase their life-skills and assertiveness in making positive choices in the utilization of Contraception, Gender Based Violence, HIV Services. The primary beneficiaries of the contribution will be young people who have been relatively left behind in terms of positive sexual reproductive health education.

Mashambanzou Care Trust-programmet syftar till att minska sårbarheten för barn i utsatthet till följd av fattigdom, HIV, TB och funktionshinder, genom att tillhandahålla socioekonomiskt och psykologiskt stöd till familjer och omgivningen. Programmet riktar sig specifikt till mycket utsatta och fattiga personer, vilket inkluderar hushåll som leds av mor/farföräldrar, barn, kvinnor samt andra utsatta hushåll. Insatsen ökar medvetenheten och främjar barns rättigheter samt prioriterar barns behov inom hälso- och sjukvården. Programmet riktar sig också till fattiga områden, särskilt HIV-smittade tonåringar som har dålig tillgång till sexuell reproduktiv hälsa och hiv-tjänster, delvis på grund av stigma, otillräckligt stöd från sjukvårdspersonal och fattigdom. Detta program kommer att sträva efter att förbättra sexuell reproduktiv hälsa genom att stärka institutionens tillhandahållande av SRHR för både HIV-smittade unga män och kvinnor för att öka deras livsfärdigheter och självförtroende när det gäller val i användningen av preventivmedel, könsbaserat våld, HIV-tjänster. De främsta förmånstagarna av bidraget kommer att vara ungdomar som har blivit relativt eftersatta vad gäller positiv utbildning i sexuell reproduktiv hälsa.

Overall Goal is: Improved access to SRHR, Health Care and Rights by 2025.
Objectives of the intervention include;
1. Improved access to integrated HIV and AIDS, care and support serices to PLWH.
2. Improved access to comprehensive Sexual Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) Services to PLWH and their families through the family centred approach.
3. Improved income earning capacity and nutrition for PLWH.
4. Improved access to ecuation, protection and nutritional support amongst children in need.

Objective 1: Improved access to integrated HIV and AIDS care and support services
Admissions and Care 631 bedridden AIDS patients admitted for palliative and HIV care, including adolescents, minors and vulnerable individuals. 349 patients discharged in good health and 185 referred for specialist care.
Family Assessments and Support 703 family assessments conducted, with individualised care plans developed for all admitted patients. 645 family members reached through family visits and discharge planning support.
Screening and Psychosocial Support 407 patients screened for mental health conditions and provided with psychosocial support. 1,052 people tested for HIV through facility and outreach testing campaigns. 300 women screened for cervical cancer, with positive cases treated or referred for specialist care.
Commemorations and Awareness Community awareness activities conducted during World AIDS Day, 16 Days of Activism Against GBV, Day of the African Child and Volunteers Day.
Objective 2: Improved access to comprehensive SRHR services through a Family-Centred Approach SRHR Activities
SRHR education sessions conducted with adolescents in Mbare, Glen Norah, Tafara and Highfields. Soccer and netball tournaments used as edutainment platforms to promote HIV prevention, life skills and positive behaviour change. No reported teen pregnancies or school dropouts among participating adolescents during Year 1. 750 adolescent girls received menstrual health packs to support menstrual hygiene and school participation.
Objective 3: Improved income earning capacity and nutrition for PLWHIV
Income Generating Activities (IGAs) 11 discharged PLWHIV beneficiaries received IGA starter packs for small businesses and vending activities. 3 monitoring visits conducted to assess business progress and provide mentorship support.
Business Management Training Beneficiaries trained in business management, proposal writing and record-keeping through a two-day entrepreneurship workshop.
Objective 4: Improved access to education, protection and nutritional support for children in need Nutrition Support
A market garden and orchard established to provide vegetables and fruits for Care Unit patients and vulnerable children.
Safe Houses and Child Protection 58 vulnerable children accommodated at Mlambo and Zata Houses of Safety, where they received meals, psychosocial support and protection services. 25 children successfully reunified with their families after temporary placement.
Birth Registration 56 children supported to obtain birth certificates, improving access to education and social services.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
